newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-firm - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-firm - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to firm amid ideas that packer demand would be strong for hogs to fill slaughter needs for Friday and Saturday, livestock dealers said.

Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to the plant could range from $56.50 to $57.00 per cwt, unchanged from Wednesday. However, if demand is strong, prices could rally $1.00, some sources said.
Illinois prices at plants were expected to match Wednesday's top of $56.00, but also could be higher if hog marketings are light, dealers there said.
Indiana and Ohio top hog prices also were expected unchanged at $56.00 at packing plants.

Strong pork movement was stoking packer demand, but the start of harvesting in the Midwest has occupied producers' time and slowed hog marketings, thereby creating brisk competition for available supplies, sources said.
However, forecasts for widespread rainfall in the Corn Belt overnight and into the weekend could result in larger hog runs as growers are rained out of their fields.
